title: Primary Function
learningObjectives: Connect cable-machine operation to pulley load transfer.
student: State the primary function of the cable machine and the adjustable pulley assembly.
instructor: The machine provides selectable resistance. The adjustable pulley redirects cable tension while its axle transfers pulley load into the bracket and frame.

title: Loading Scenarios
learningObjectives: Classify the three physical loading scenarios.
student: Classify pulley self-weight, normal full-stack exercise, and the amplified transient event as dead, live, or accidental loading. Explain each choice.
instructor: Pulley self-weight is permanent dead load in the local model. Normal exercise is live load. The amplified abnormal/transient event is accidental loading. The selectable weight stack is not dead load.

title: External Loads
learningObjectives: Identify forces on pulley and axle.
student: Identify the external forces acting on the selected pulley and axle.
instructor: Two equal cable tensions act on the pulley at the included angle theta. Their vector resultant loads the pulley; the axle/bracket reaction balances it. The pulley transmits an equal-and-opposite force to the axle.

title: Supports and Boundary Conditions
learningObjectives: Relate two bracket plates to two shear planes.
student: Describe how the two bracket plates support the axle and why the simplified connection has two shear planes.
instructor: The pulley lies between two supporting plates. The axle crosses both plate interfaces, so the idealized load transfer acts across two pin sections in double shear.

title: Load Path
learningObjectives: Trace force from weight stack to frame.
student: Trace the load path from the selected weight stack through the cable, pulley, axle, bracket or carriage, and machine frame.
instructor: The load path is weight stack to cable to pulley to pulley axle to bracket/carriage to machine frame.

title: Critical Component
student: Identify the analyzed component and explain why it is a useful Mechanics of Materials connection problem.
instructor: The circular pulley axle is analyzed because it transfers the resultant pulley load into two supporting plates and can be idealized as a double-shear pin.

title: Relevant Mechanical Response
learningObjectives: Distinguish average shear from omitted responses.
student: Identify the primary response evaluated here and distinguish it from bearing, axle bending, fatigue, and local bracket effects.
instructor: The included response is average direct shear over two axle planes. Bearing, bending, fatigue, local contact, and bracket effects require separate models.

title: Relevant Parameters
learningObjectives: Identify the six editable inputs and fixed g.
student: Identify the quantities needed to calculate cable tension, force resultant, double-shear area, and average shear stress.
instructor: The editable inputs are m_s, r, m_p, d, theta, and k_d. Gravitational acceleration is fixed at 9.81 m/s^2.

title: Student-Generated Idealization
learningObjectives: Construct compatible pulley and axle models.
student: Draw a pulley free-body diagram with two equal tension vectors separated by the included angle theta. Separately draw the circular axle between two bracket plates with two idealized shear planes.
instructor: A complete model defines theta between the two tension vectors, shows their resultant at the pulley center, and shows the axle crossing two bracket interfaces in double shear.

title: Modeling Assumptions and Plan
student: State the simplifying assumptions and outline the analysis sequence before substituting numbers.
instructor: Assume ideal bearings, equal cable tensions, the assigned ideal ratio and angle, average double shear, equal bracket sharing, small deformation, and static-equivalent loading. Then calculate dead weight, live and accidental tensions/resultants, axle areas, three stresses, and the governing case.

title: Loading Classification
student: For each specified scenario, explain why it is treated as dead, live, or accidental loading.
instructor: Dead load is the permanent pulley self-weight. Live load is normal full-stack exercise. Accidental load is the simplified abnormal/transient case represented by k_d. These names do not describe axial, bending, or torsional response.

title: Dead Load
student: Using the pulley mass and fixed gravitational acceleration, determine the permanent gravitational load carried by the axle in the local model.
instructor: W_p = m_p g = {{pulley_Wp_N}} N.

title: Live-Load Cable Tension
student: Determine the ideal cable tension for normal full-stack operation.
instructor: T_L = m_s g/r = {{pulley_TL_N}} N.

title: Live-Load Pulley Resultant
student: Using the included angle theta between two equal tension vectors, determine the magnitude and direction of the live-load resultant transmitted through the pulley.
instructor: R_L = sqrt(T_L^2 + T_L^2 + 2T_L^2 cos theta) = {{pulley_RL_N}} N. {{pulley_resultant_direction}}

title: Accidental Cable Tension
student: Apply the assigned dynamic coefficient to determine the simplified accidental/transient cable tension.
instructor: T_A = k_d T_L = {{pulley_TA_N}} N.

title: Accidental Pulley Resultant
learningObjectives: Calculate the accidental resultant at general theta.
student: Determine the corresponding accidental/transient force-resultant magnitude using the same included angle.
instructor: R_A = sqrt(T_A^2 + T_A^2 + 2T_A^2 cos theta) = {{pulley_RA_N}} N.

title: Axle Shear Area
student: Calculate the circular axle area A and the total resisting area A_s for idealized double shear.
instructor: A = pi d^2/4 = {{pulley_A_mm2}} mm2; A_s = 2A = {{pulley_As_mm2}} mm2.

title: Average Shear Stress - Dead
student: Determine average axle double-shear stress from pulley self-weight.
instructor: tau_D = W_p/(2A) = {{pulley_tauD_MPa}} MPa.

title: Average Shear Stress - Live
student: Determine average axle double-shear stress for normal operation.
instructor: tau_L = R_L/(2A) = {{pulley_tauL_MPa}} MPa.

title: Average Shear Stress - Accidental
student: Determine average axle double-shear stress for the accidental/transient case.
instructor: tau_A = R_A/(2A) = {{pulley_tauA_MPa}} MPa. The ratio tau_A/tau_L is {{pulley_dynamic_ratio}}.

title: Engineering Assessment
learningObjectives: Identify the governing scenario without claiming safety.
student: Compare all three stresses, identify the governing loading scenario, and explain why this result alone cannot certify the real connection as safe.
instructor: {{pulley_governing_case}} governs the included cases at {{pulley_governing_tau_MPa}} MPa. {{pulley_assessment}}
